title: Infrastructure incident postmortem — timeline, technical, corrections
raw: okay incident postmortem notes for the outage on june fifteenth so the timeline is at approximately two seventeen am pdt our monitoring picked up elevated error rates on the api gateway and at two twenty three am the on call engineer no wait it was two twenty one because i'm looking at the pagerduty log and alex got paged at two twenty one and acknowledged at two twenty four and by two thirty five we had identified the root cause which was a memory leak in the new version of the recommendation service that was deployed at eleven pm the night before and the fix was straightforward we rolled back to the previous version at two forty nine am and error rates returned to normal by two fifty seven so total downtime was forty no thirty six minutes from first alert to resolution and the affected services were the recommendation api the home feed and the notifications service and we estimate roughly twelve thousand users were affected based on traffic during that window and the action items are one add memory limits to the recommendation service deployment config two add a canary deployment step so we catch this kind of regression before it hits prod three fix the alerting because our memory threshold alert was set too high at ninety percent it should be seventy five and four do a proper load test of the recommendation service before the next release
reference: Incident postmortem — June 15 outage. Timeline (PDT): at 2:17 AM, monitoring picked up elevated error rates on the API gateway. Alex was paged at 2:21 AM and acknowledged at 2:24 AM. By 2:35 AM we identified the root cause — a memory leak in the new version of the recommendation service, which was deployed at 11 PM the night before. We rolled back to the previous version at 2:49 AM. Error rates returned to normal by 2:57 AM. Total downtime: 36 minutes from first alert to resolution. Affected services: recommendation API, home feed, notifications. Roughly 12,000 users were affected. Action items: (1) add memory limits to the recommendation service deployment config, (2) add a canary deployment step to catch regressions before they hit prod, (3) lower the memory threshold alert from 90% to 75%, and (4) do a proper load test of the recommendation service before the next release.
